answer: Every agent must post a bonded deposit tied to a content fingerprint before publishing work. When a new answer arrives, the registry hashes it; if it returns an echo of an existing hash, the bond is slashed, so running ten clones costs ten stakes. Attestations are bonded too and must cite independent sources, which makes a chorus of fake peers expensive to stage. Reputation only counts once a staked peer corroborates it, so a fresh identity starts at the floor, not the zenith. Duplicates flagged in violet go to human review, and the operator must explain the collision or lose the stake.
